items.title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
items.note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS ESTABLISHED 2026-09-21, AND IT IS A PERCENTAGE, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The operator read Settings > Usage directly. Plan: Max (20x). The surface exposes THREE meters, each a percent-of-allowance bar with no absolute number anywhere: a ~5-hour SESSION window, a WEEKLY window, and a SEPARATE WEEKLY LIMIT FOR FABLE. Anthropic's own support pages publish no figure either -- only '20x Pro per-session allowance'. [!] DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS, and this is a design decision rather than a limitation. The allowance is MODEL-WEIGHTED, so tokens-per-percent is not a constant -- it is a function of the model mix and moves whenever the manager routes a lane to sonnet instead of opus. A token budget would read as precise and drift silently. A1 METERS IN PERCENT. The operator's rule -- 10% of the weekly budget per day -- is already stated in that unit, so no conversion is needed to enforce it. A measured per-model exchange rate may be reported as a sanity check, labelled measured and drifting, NEVER as the budget. [!] TWO WINDOWS BIND, NOT ONE. The weekly cap is what the 10%/day rule governs; the ~5-hour session window is what actually walls a lane mid-run. A day's 10% spent as a single burst can exhaust the session window while the weekly meter still reads green, so A1 MUST SHOW BOTH or it reports 'fine' during an outage. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21, and it CORRECTS an earlier claim on this row that was asserted rather than checked. The claim was that a meter summing only agent lanes would systematically under-report because the operator's own chat draws on the same pool. The mechanism is real -- all surfaces do share one limit -- but the magnitude is currently ZERO: 'What's using your week' reads Claude Code 100%, Chats 0%, Cowork 0%, Other 0%. Lane accounting is therefore ~= the whole pool today. A1 should still LABEL its scope, because the day that mix changes the meter goes quietly wrong. [!] THE MANAGER'S METER IS THE **DAILY** BUDGET, NOT THE WEEKLY BAR (operator, 2026-09-21): 'the manager should be focused on the daily budget, not weekly, as I sometimes use Claude for other projects... I will start a new manager session after this one and I expect it to use the daily budget, even if we pass into the margin.' [!] THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM WRITTEN ON THIS ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY, and it is the SAME CATEGORY ERROR this row already caught once with cost_usd. That claim read: '68% of the week consumed with ~2 of 7 days left, ~13.6%/day against a 10%/day target, so THE STATED POLICY IS NOT BEING MET.' It compared TOTAL weekly consumption against the MANAGER'S daily allowance -- two different populations. The weekly bar aggregates every surface and every project the operator touches, including work this repo's manager cannot see and did not cause, so it CANNOT grade the manager. ('Claude Code 100%' does not rescue it: the operator's other projects are also Claude Code.) The 68% reading stands as a fact about the ACCOUNT; the conclusion drawn from it was unsupported and is withdrawn. [!] SO A1 REPORTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BLEND THEM. (a) THE CONTROL VARIABLE: this repo's spend today against the daily budget -- 10% of the weekly allowance. That is the number the manager is accountable for. (b) CONTEXT ONLY: the account-level weekly bar, unattributable and reported as such. A single blended 'budget' figure is the bug. [!] THE 30% WEEKLY MARGIN IS NOT A RESERVE THE MANAGER PRESERVES BY DOING LESS. It exists to absorb the operator's other projects and surprises. A manager that throttles its own lane because the ACCOUNT bar looks high is spending the margin's purpose on nothing. The operator has stated explicitly that the next manager should spend its daily budget EVEN IF that passes into the margin. [!] AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HITTING A CAP -- it is 'losing work to sessions dying in the middle' (operator). THAT IS A DURABILITY PROBLEM, NOT A BUDGET ONE, and budgeting alone cannot fix it. The mitigations are structural: land work in small PRs rather than one large one, push before you answer, and keep state on disk (PIPELINE.jsonl, the checklist) rather than in a session's head. The ~5-HOUR SESSION WINDOW is what actually kills a session mid-task, so it is the in-session number to watch; the weekly bar never killed anything mid-run. [!] FABLE HAS A SEPARATE WEEKLY ALLOWANCE, MEASURED AT 0% USED, AND THE OPERATOR HAS DIRECTED THAT IT BE EMPLOYED (2026-09-21): 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' It is a SECOND pool that does not draw on the main one, so work routed there is additive capacity, not a trade-off. That makes it a live routing input for the model table in .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. Tracked as E11 -- A1 reports the pool, E11 decides what goes in it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 alongside A3a rather than before it, because A3a was told to render section 5 WITHOUT the spend figures (it already has the unrouted count from pipeline.py) and to print an explicit 'not measured -- A1 not built' line. So the blocked_on edge is narrower than it read: section 5 ships either way and A1 fills it in. FRESH, sonnet-5. [!] THE QUESTION PUT TO THE LANE is deliberately not 'build a cost meter' but 'what does section 5 print on a day nobody has read the usage meter' -- because the denominator is not machine-readable and the failure mode on this row has twice been a figure that looked precise and was not. [!] BUILT 2026-09-21, PR #12683 open (draft, not merged -- state stays `in_flight` until the manager merges it; move to `landed_unproven` on merge, and `done` only once A3a's section-5 wiring is observed calling this module in a real brief): `scripts/ops/spend_meter.py` -- an append-only on-disk record of operator-entered readings (session/weekly/fable_weekly, percent + read_at) and `render_section_5()` for A3a to call. Verified this session: a day with no reading prints `never recorded` per window (never `0%`); a stale reading always renders its age and is never presented as current; per-lane `cost_usd` is reachable only from an interactive session holding `get_session`/`list_sessions` -- confirmed by calling those tools directly against this session and its parent manager -- and NOT from a CI runner or a Routine-fired turn (reconfirms, does not re-derive, the same finding already in `render_daily_brief.py` and `queue_latency.py`); no CI-reachable credential for it exists in this repo (checked: `.github/workflows/`, `docs/reference/env-vars.md`, `docs/claude/system-actions.md`). NOT yet wired into the real daily brief -- that is A3a's job, out of this row's scope fence. [!] MERGED 2026-09-21 as 9e9fb3a. ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED 6.86 -> 28.03: the earlier figure was read MID-FLIGHT and left on the row looking like a total. A meter's own row reporting a stale number is the failure the meter exists to prevent. [!] ⚠️ SPEND CORRECTED AGAIN, READ AFTER ARCHIVING: $59.17. The figure committed hours earlier was ALSO mid-flight. [!] ⚠️ STATE CORRECTED BY THE LANE, NOT BY THE MANAGER (#12698): this row was marked `done` on the strength of #12683 merging, and the lane read origin/main:scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py directly and found §5 STILL PRINTING `A1 (cost meter) is not built`. The meter is built, tested, guard-registered -- and nothing calls it. Merged is not deployed is not observed, and this row had collapsed the first into the third on the manager's say-so. [!] CLOSING THIS ROW MEANS: a real daily brief whose §5 prints a spend figure sourced from `spend_meter.render_section_5` -- not the placeholder `A1 (cost meter) is not built`, and not a hand-run of the module. The wiring is in `render_daily_brief.py`; re-reading `spend_meter.py` proves nothing, because the module was never the gap.

items.title: armed-branch-push-watch races PR creation — every post-merge follow-up trips it
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-21 on PR #12673, which is the follow-up to the reset's own merge. scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py reported `dropped` (error, exit 1) on a HEALTHY push. Timing is the whole bug: #12668 squash-merged as 3ea2777 at 12:18 and GitHub deleted the branch; the branch was reset from the new main and A6 pushed at 12:25:43; #12673 was opened at 12:26:10. The watcher ran in that 27-second gap, when the branch's ONLY associated PR was the merged #12668 whose head.sha (1d596e2) is not the pushed sha (f3301d0). [!] THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. A PR cannot be opened for a branch that has not been pushed, so EVERY follow-up PR made the sanctioned way (git fetch origin main && git checkout -B <branch> origin/main) trips this between push and PR creation. The guard's premise -- that the PR it finds is the PR for this push -- is false during a branch reset. [!] DO NOT 'FIX' IT BY DOWNGRADING THE SEVERITY. The loss it exists for (#11846) is real, and a guard that cries wolf on the healthy path is how a guard gets ignored -- the desensitisation this repo already measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched condition. Sharpen the condition. [!] THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it does NOT fall into the ancestry trap the script's own docstring warns about. That trap is asking whether a BRANCH commit reached main -- which a squash merge always answers no to. Ask the OPPOSITE: is the old PR's MERGE COMMIT an ancestor of the PUSHED commit? Branch correctly reset -> yes (3ea2777 is an ancestor of f3301d0), nothing lost, a new PR is coming. Genuine drop, i.e. more commits pushed onto the merged branch's old history -> no; the pre-merge head is the ancestor instead. A squash does not defeat that direction. [!] The script has an elaborate --self-test with a mutation-tested exact-sha comparison; extend it rather than loosening it, and add the branch-reset case as a NAMED fixture so the next person cannot re-introduce this by tightening something else. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21, sonnet-5, fresh, ceiling $12 (this row carried no ceiling; one is set now). It earns its slot today because the manager's own pushes are the population it mis-grades: every follow-up PR made the sanctioned way trips it in the gap between push and PR creation. Lane told in terms to SHARPEN the condition and NOT downgrade the severity, and to CONSTRUCT both cases rather than implement the proposed discriminator on trust -- a reported hole beats a confident fix. [!] CLOSED 2026-09-21 AS ALREADY FIXED, AND THE LANE THAT ESTABLISHED IT WAS DISPATCHED IN ERROR BY THIS MANAGER. The fix landed in #12676 -- the SAME PR the handoff named as 'A7's pipeline + close-out contract + E10' -- and this row was never moved off `queued`. VERIFIED on main, not taken from the lane: scripts/ci/check_armed_branch_push.py defines RESET_FROM_MERGE, carries the merge-commit-ancestry discriminator, and has the branch-reset case as a named self-test fixture. Cost of the error: $0.93. [!] THE LESSON IS NOT 'READ MORE CAREFULLY', it is that a row's `state` was not moved by the PR that resolved it, so the register lied to the next reader in the direction of MORE work rather than less. Filed as PI-20260921-M06.

items.title: The exit monitor's registry-failure fallback covers 0 of 52 routed-live legs
items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by parsing config/strategies.yaml (55 declared) + config/accounts.yaml (11 accounts) at 0d3ab95: 52 distinct strategies are routed to at least one `mode: live` account. src/runtime/pipeline.py:349-351 returns the hardcoded fallback ['turtle_soup','vwap'] whenever load_strategies() raises. NEITHER name is routed to any live account -- turtle_soup is `execution: shadow`, vwap is `enabled: false` + `execution: shadow`. The set difference is 52 of 52. [!] THIS IS NOT ONLY AN ENTRY-SIDE LIST. `STRATEGIES` is what the EXIT half iterates: run_exit_evaluation_tick calls _load_strategies(None) -> pipeline.STRATEGIES, then get_order_packages_by_strategy per name. On the fallback, every open package belonging to the other 52 legs receives NO monitor() call -- no trailing amend, no stale-exit, no giveback stop, no exit head. Open REAL-MONEY positions would sit unmanaged until a broker-side bracket or the reconciler caught them. [!] THE TRIGGER IS REACHABLE. STRATEGIES is a module-level constant evaluated once at import and the fallback fires on ANY load_strategies() exception -- a malformed config/strategies.yaml being the live one. ict-git-sync pulls main every ~5 min, so a YAML syntax error landing on main reaches the live trader inside ~5 minutes. [!] AND IT IS SILENT. One logger.warning at import. None of the health snapshot's 7 checks (service, git_drift, git_fetch, tick, accounts_api, db, disk) would go red -- the process is alive, ticking, in sync, and the DB answers. The snapshot keeps reading `7/7 checks ok`. [!] FIELD BEATS COMMENT: the comment at pipeline.py:350 asserts the fallback `matches the production roster in config/strategies.yaml after PR B1`. Measured today it matches 0 of 52 -- the same shape as the trainer flock comment fixed in de20550. [!] SECOND, SEPARATE COLLAPSE at order_monitor.py:124-126: _load_strategies returns [] on exception, and the tick then returns {} summaries -- `we could not resolve the strategy list` and `no strategy had anything open` are indistinguishable downstream. [!] PROPOSED FIX, not applied (Tier-2, and /health-review may not touch src/): (1) delete the VALUE fallback -- on registry failure raise, or return a sentinel callers must branch on; a trader that cannot read its own roster must not silently run a two-name one. (2) Make the exit half's population open-package-driven (SELECT DISTINCT strategy FROM order_packages WHERE status='open') UNION the roster, so an open position is monitored because it IS OPEN, never because it appears in a list. (3) Add a health check comparing len(STRATEGIES) against the enabled count in strategies.yaml. [!] REFUTED HYPOTHESIS, recorded so it is not re-derived: the TLT position open on alpaca_live (id 5924, pattern tlt_pullback_1h, opened 2026-09-18) belongs to a leg A6/#12673 pulled from the alpaca_live ROSTER on 2026-09-21, and is NOT stranded -- exit evaluation iterates the strategies.yaml registry, not account rosters, and tlt_pullback_1h is still enabled there (r-block updated 05:29Z). Roster removal does not strand an open position; registry FAILURE would strand all of them. [!] LANE session_014LSHstYGrXDTZnNW5kgjn8, 2026-09-22, branch `e21-exit-monitor-roster-resolution`. RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY rather than inherited, by parsing config/strategies.yaml (55 declared) + config/accounts.yaml (11 accounts) at f3746ab: 52 distinct strategies routed to >=1 `mode: live` account; the fallback covered 0 of 52; turtle_soup `execution: shadow`, vwap `enabled: false` + `execution: shadow`. The review's numbers hold. That re-measurement is now a TEST (tests/test_e21_exit_roster_resolution.py::test_the_retired_fallback_covered_no_live_leg), so the comment cannot drift from the config again. [!] DECIDED (this lane, arguing the question the dispatch posed): THE ENTRY AND EXIT SIDES GET DIFFERENT ANSWERS, because the question 'fall back to a list, or refuse' is only hard while the exit half depends on that list. (1) ENTRY: no value fallback at all. `resolve_roster()` returns a three-state resolution (ok/empty/unreadable) and `STRATEGIES` is EMPTY on `unreadable`, so the trader opens nothing rather than opening the wrong two names. This is NOT the trader switching itself off (Prime Directive rule 2): no account `mode:` is written, no breaker latches, the process keeps ticking and comes up live on the next boot per YAML; it is a per-condition refusal with a logged cause, the same shape as `pipeline.strategy_builders()`, which is deliberately un-wrapped on the stated ground that 'a rollback that cannot resolve its roster must fail loudly rather than resolve to an empty dict and silently trade nothing'. And the old fallback was ALREADY a near-total entry halt -- 0 of 52 -- only a silent one that additionally re-enabled two deliberately non-executing legs. (2) EXIT: does not consult the roster state to decide what to monitor AT ALL. `order_monitor.exit_population()` is `SELECT DISTINCT strategy_name FROM order_packages WHERE status='open'` UNION the roster, in roster order. A position is monitored because it is OPEN. That is what makes (1) safe: refusing to open new positions no longer costs exit management of the open ones. [!] REQUIREMENT 3 (positions whose leg left the roster) IS ADDRESSED, AND THE ROW'S OWN REFUTED HYPOTHESIS IS CONFIRMED CORRECT rather than re-derived: exit evaluation never read ACCOUNT rosters, so A6/#12673 removing tlt_pullback_1h from alpaca_live's roster did not strand the open TLT position -- VERIFIED this session by reading src/strategy_registry.py::load_strategies, which does not filter on `enabled` or `execution` and returns all 55 declared names, and run_exit_evaluation_tick, which iterates that list. THE RESIDUAL GAP IS REGISTRY REMOVAL, NOT ROSTER REMOVAL: a leg deleted from strategies.yaml (or the whole file becoming unreadable) while holding an open position WAS stranded, and row R2 cuts four more legs. The union closes that, and is pinned end-to-end by test_exit_tick_scans_an_open_package_off_the_roster, which drives a real sqlite journal through run_exit_evaluation_tick. [!] REQUIREMENT 2 (not silent): new health check `strategy_roster` in src/runtime/health.py, added to _DEFAULT_CHECKS so the snapshot carries 8 rather than 7. `unreadable` and `empty` are BOTH critical and carry DIFFERENT ctx.state + detail -- the collapsed-state standard is that they must not render identically, not that they must grade differently. Registered as contract `strategy_roster.roster_state` in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py; the guard reports `3 consumer(s), all states read`. The check re-reads the YAML through `strategy_registry.reload_strategies()` because the registry caches after first load -- without that bypass the check would answer from the last good read forever and could never fire, which is pinned by test_health_check_rereads_the_file_rather_than_a_cached_roster. [!] PROOF THE TESTS ARE A REGRESSION TEST AND NOT DECORATION: 11 tests, all passing on the branch. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-22 by this lane, direct against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org, with a positive control in the same run: CONTROL unit=ict-web-api.service -> HTTP 200 with 3 journal lines; unit=ssh / ssh.service / sshd / sshd.service -> HTTP 400 `unknown_unit` on all four. The counts-only summariser and dropping the requirement were both offered and both declined. The privacy cost was stated in the question and accepted: sshd journal lines carry source IPs and usernames, and every session that can reach /api/diag/* will be able to read them. [!] THE UNIT NAME WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THE ALIAS IS A TRAP. Allowlisting the alias would have answered HTTP 200 with `lines: []` and `available: true`, i.e. a breach sweep reporting CLEAN having read nothing -- worse than the 400. `ssh.service` is the ONLY entry added and the test pins both halves (ssh.service accepted, sshd.service still 400). DUAL USE CHECKED BEFORE PUSHING: _CANONICAL_UNITS is read at four other sites, all inside diag.py -- /snapshot and /services REPORT systemctl state from it (they assert nothing) and _timer_units() filters to `.timer`. Every reference outside diag.py is a comment, except scripts/check_diag_unit_allowlist.py, which checks the OTHER direction (every deploy/ unit is queryable) and passes unchanged: 47 scanned, 41 allowlisted, 8 exempted, 0 failures. No liveness surface starts asserting on ssh.service. items.title: The eight ict_scalp_* legs route to no harness — the same defect E25 just fixed for fvg_range, at eight times the size
items.note:
OPENED 2026-09-22 off E25's finding (#12714). WORKED 2026-09-22 by this lane on branch e28-ict-scalp-harness-route.

[!] IT IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS E25, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE ROW. E25 added a classifier branch and a lever map to a harness that already took every parameter on the command line. backtest_ict_scalp.py declares NO flag for any of the fourteen keys src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py::_DEFAULTS consumes, so the '--ignore-yaml and forward every param' half of this row's design call DOES NOT EXIST -- read off the harness's own add_argument list, not its docstring. The YAML read is load-bearing. AND the other half was UNSOUND AS SHIPPED: _load_yaml_params() read the ict_scalp_5m block for every leg (MI-321 measured this on 2026-09-18 and filed it explicitly unfixed, the file being outside that lane's Tier-1 surface; MI-242 has since put scripts/backtest_*.py inside it). Routing eight legs at the old signature would have measured ONE leg's config eight times under eight names and written eight coverage_state=measured records -- strictly worse than the no_harness they replace, because a wrong number reads as evidence and a missing one does not. So the design call resolved to: FIX THE READ FIRST (--strategy-name now selects the block and RAISES on an unknown name), then trust it, and forward only the levers the YAML read cannot reach (the exit levers and the HTF geometry, which are run_backtest KEYWORDS rather than cfg keys, plus --sim-breakeven, which the live monitor genuinely arms from be_offset_bps).

SOL is the controlled comparison -- identical params, identical symbol: 5m is -14.7099 over n=258, 15m is +4.0692 over n=133. XRP the same: -8.2061/n=245 vs +1.1225/n=130. EN ROUTE, A SECOND DEFECT ONLY THIS CHANGE MADE REACHABLE (E25's own pattern). mgc is the one non-USDT leg, so this is the first time anything asked Yahoo for 15m over 365d. items.note: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by me while landing the merge wave. POPULATION: the 100 most recent COMPLETED workflow runs on `main`, window 06:38:10Z -> 07:53:57Z (every push of this session's merge wave), across 53 distinct workflows. RESULT: 2 of 53 fail, and BOTH fail 6 of 6 with ZERO successes -- `reconcile-open-prs` and `work-digest`. [!] A THIRD, `merge-claim-audit`, fails on PR heads rather than on main, OBSERVED on 8867208 at 07:52Z. [!] THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS AS E23 AND E27, AND THEY ARE NOW FOUR INSTANCES IN ONE DAY, EACH FOUND INDEPENDENTLY: the reset archived registers and nothing swept the workflows, guards and skills that read them. [!] UPPER BOUND, EXPLICITLY NOT A DEFECT COUNT: scanning 562 source files under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills (pycache excluded) for repo-relative path literals, 137 distinct paths DO NOT EXIST on disk, and 34 workflows name at least one. That number is NOT 137 bugs -- many are files the naming workflow PRODUCES (the econ-calendar and macro backfills are the obvious ones), so the deliverable is a TRIAGE separating `reads a file that must pre-exist` from `writes it`, then fixing the first set. Do not sweep on the raw count. SCOPE: fix the three named failures first, since those are observed red, then triage the rest and file what is left. [!] ================ E29 BUILD LANE, 2026-09-22 — PR #12719 (DRAFT, landing: hold) ================ [!] WORK-DIGEST'S CAUSE IS NOW ESTABLISHED, and the row was right to refuse to guess it: it is NOT the same as the other two. `python3 scripts/ops/work_digest.py --self-test` fails check 10 (`every declared source exists on disk`) naming FIVE archived registers -- docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json and ALL FOUR docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json. Established by RUNNING the self-test on the checkout, not by reading a log. [!] AND THE RED CI IS THE SMALLER HALF OF THAT FINDING: five of the digest's six declared sources have read `absent` on EVERY run from the reset onward, so the work digest has been structurally blind to five-sixths of its inputs while reporting itself healthy. The three causes re-verified by running each failing step on the checkout rather than trusting this row. [!] DISPOSITIONS, EACH DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED TO REPAIR. (1) merge-claim-audit RETIRED: it audits the merge-slot claim protocol on the coordination board the reset retired. The repair WAS available and was rejected on its merits -- board_pointer.py accepts `board_state: "retired"`, so a tombstone pointer makes the self-test pass; that is a workflow running on every merge to say `there is no board`. Its stated purpose was to build ONE number (how often an unclaimed merge coincides with a real collision) to decide whether to enforce, and with no board that number can never be collected. (2) reconcile-open-prs RETIRED: its register is archived. (3) work-digest REPAIRED, not retired: the five dead sources are cut and MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json -- THE register under the reset's own `one register` model -- remains, so the digest now watches exactly the surface the operating model says work lives on. Triggers are COMMENTED OUT rather than the files deleted: check_workflow_catalog.py pins every workflow to a catalogue row in both directions, and each file's rationale is a decision record. Both catalogue rows updated. [!] THE 14 OPEN PRs ARE ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS CLOSE THEM, NOT MERGE THEM -- MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. #12451…#12511, opened 2026-09-17T15:30Z … 2026-09-18T04:47Z. (a) Every branch is cut from a PRE-RESET main: `git diff --stat main <branch>` gives 1,055 files / 315,876 deletions on the newest (#12511) and 1,190 / 394,616 on the oldest (#12451), so MERGING ANY ONE REVERTS THE OPERATING RESET WHOLESALE. (b) Nothing is lost by closing them: their only payload is OPEN-PRS.json (the job's `paths:` names that file alone) and it is strictly STALER than the archived copy -- branch 9 open / 114 settled against the archive's 12 / 118, and #12400, the one number the branch has that the archive's open_prs lacks, sits in the archive's settled_prs, i.e. already reconciled. (c) The known drop hazard does NOT apply: sweep_stale_automation_prs.py warns that closing a WORK-DIGEST PR drops queued pending-pings.jsonl rows; these are not work-digest PRs and carry no ping payload. [!] I DID NOT CLOSE THEM. Fourteen closes are outward-facing and the lane's dispatch says push, open a draft, update the row, STOP. Filed as PI-20260922-RECONCILE-OPEN-PRS-14-STRANDED-PRS-NEED-CLOSING-NOT-MERGING. MANAGER: this is the one action this row leaves undone that has a live footgun behind it. [!] THE SHAPE FIX, WHICH OUTLASTS ALL THREE. `open_pr_record.read_record()` reported an ABSENT file as `(None, readable=True)` -- `the register is gone` and `the register read fine` were the SAME VALUE, which is why the failure arrived as a stack trace instead of as a finding. Added `read_record_state()` returning `absent | read | unreadable`, with read_record() now defined in terms of it so the two cannot drift, and a FOURTH verdict `register_absent` on the reconciler that EXITS 0 AND SAYS THE FILE IS MISSING. A fourth state rather than a flavour of could_not_look, deliberately: absent and present-but-unreadable are opposite findings with opposite remedies. [!] A JOB THAT EXITS CLEAN HAVING SILENTLY DONE NOTHING WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORSE FIX, so the test asserts absent AGAINST A PRESENT-AND-EMPTY POSITIVE CONTROL rather than merely that the crash is gone. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY CONTROLS WHILE FIXING, NEITHER BY INSPECTION, AND BOTH WORTH THE ROW. (i) read_record's `path=RECORD_PATH` default BOUND AT IMPORT, so repointing RECORD_PATH was silently ignored and the function read the original file while appearing to honour the override -- caught only because the new test carried a positive control. Now resolved at call time. (ii) tests/test_work_digest.py::test_editing_a_backlog_row_without_closing_it_is_activity had gone VACUOUS AND STAYED GREEN: it asserts `events == []`, which an unwatched path satisfies for entirely the wrong reason. The differ tests now declare their own fixture registers so they cannot pass because the roster moved, and the roster test itself was rewritten -- it USED TO REQUIRE OPEN-ITEMS.json, which is how a roster test outlives its roster. [!] THE TRIAGE, AND IT CHANGES THE PROPOSED REMEDY RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT. The 137 figure is an upper bound and re-running that shape is NOT a usable detector: my own first pass produced 216 and was dominated by noise -- an extension-ordering bug splitting .jsonl as .json, self-test fixture literals, docstring prose, and files the naming workflow PRODUCES. THE DECIDABLE SIGNAL IS NARROWER: a path the reset ARCHIVED that a live source still names. MEASURED: 289 paths archived and still absent, 40 of them STILL NAMED by live sources under .github/workflows, scripts/ci, scripts/ops and .claude/skills -- health-review-backlog.json 31 namers, OPEN-ITEMS.json 25, ml-review-backlog.json 25, performance-review-backlog.json 23, SESSIONS.json 16, research-review-backlog.json 15, board-pointer.json 12. [!] THE PROBE HAS ONE TRAP AND IT SILENTLY REPORTS ALL-CLEAR: the reset RENAMED files into docs/archive/, so `git diff --diff-filter=D` returns ZERO and only `--no-renames` sees them. I hit that and caught it on a positive control. PROPOSED REMEDY: one guard keyed on archived-and-still-referenced, shipped REPORT-ONLY against a declared baseline that shrinks, NEVER blocking -- 40 paths across ~60 files would go red on every PR at once and a guard nobody can go green against gets waived rather than satisfied. IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL FOUR OF THE DAY'S INSTANCES: E23 (and its three unfixed sibling skills), E27, and all three of this row's workflows. Filed as PI-20260922-ARCHIVED-REGISTERS-STILL-READ-BY-40-PATHS-ACROSS-LIVE-CI-SOURCES. [!] NOT DONE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (1) The board family -- board-heartbeat.yml, board-post.yml, board-rotate.yml, scope-overlap-audit.yml, pr-close.yml -- still resolves through the absent pointer. NONE is red, and that is NOT because they are healthy: parsing each `on:` block, heartbeat and scope-overlap are workflow_dispatch ONLY, and board-post/board-rotate fire only on pushes to automation/board-*/** which nothing writes now. They are DORMANT, and each goes red the moment it is dispatched. That is one decision about the family, not five patches. (2) PIPELINE.jsonl is still not a digest source -- it is append-only JSONL, not a keyed register, so _items_at() cannot diff it, and until that lands a pipeline item coming due produces NO PING. (3) Six modules still call the two-state read_record() and treat absent as empty; the collapse is now pinned by a test so a future edit has to mean it. [!] VERIFICATION, run on the checkout: work_digest --self-test PASS (was FAIL), with a NEGATIVE CONTROL -- restoring a retired register to disk makes new check 11b FAIL, removing it restores PASS, so the new check has teeth. reconcile_open_prs.py --json now prints state=register_absent, exit 0, naming the file and the archive path. check_workflow_catalog.py OK (143 workflows, both directions). items.title: The paper books' P&L is mostly NOT measured, which is the stage that exists to measure realized cost
items.note: OPENED 2026-09-22 by the manager. The 2026-09-22 /health-review graded `data_validity` as `watch` and named these figures, but the finding was left in the review JSON and NEVER became a row -- so by the close-out skill's own test it was not filed. This row is that filing. MEASURED LIVE by me at 2026-09-22T09:1x from GET /api/bot/stats, and the numbers have MOVED since the review (paper 264/658 -> 266/661), so this is ongoing, not a stale snapshot: real book pnlCoverage 0.7633 with pnlMeasuredCount 329 / pnlEstimatedCount 20; PAPER book pnlCoverage 0.2235 with pnlMeasuredCount 266 / pnlEstimatedCount 661. [!] WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: under the promotion ladder, Stage 1 (bybit_1 / alpaca_paper) exists to answer exactly one question -- `do the mechanics work, and does REALIZED COST match what the backtest assumed`. A book whose P&L is predominantly ESTIMATED cannot answer a question about REALIZED cost. So Gate 1's instrument may be reading its own reconstruction rather than the venue, and E3's whole point was that the backtests were fee-only and optimistic by an unknown amount. If the paper book that is supposed to check that assumption is itself largely estimated, the check is weaker than anyone has stated. [!] WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, STATED SO NOBODY QUOTES A NUMBER I DID NOT VERIFY: the DENOMINATOR of pnlCoverage. 266/(266+661) = 0.287, which is NOT the 0.2235 the field reports, so coverage is computed over a larger population than measured+estimated -- there is at least a third bucket (plausibly UNVERIFIED per src/runtime/provenance.py, which the rules say is never folded into measured). Do not restate 'the paper book is 78% estimated' until that denominator is read from the code. FIRST TASK OF THIS ROW IS TO ESTABLISH IT. [!] THEN: find out WHY the paper legs' fills are not measured when the real book's are (broker fill records absent for paper accounts? a different write path? an ingest that never ran?), and say whether it is fixable or structural. If structural, the honest outcome is a stated limit on what Gate 1 can conclude -- which is worth more than a fix that is not available.

items.title: The prop bar is an EXPECTED-VALUE question, not a drawdown-avoidance one — and the corpus cannot answer it
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22, and it REPLACES the bar I proposed an hour earlier: 'it's ok if there is ever breach, the idea is that we want to promote strategies that create a portfolio that we would statistically expect to produce a profit (over the initial account cost of about 1%) before the account dies - that is the basis for building the prop portfolio.' [!] SO THE PROP BAR IS: E[profit before the account dies] > the account cost. Breach is an ACCEPTED, EXPECTED outcome -- the cost of the bet -- not a failure to prevent. This is a ruin-WITH-PAYOFF problem and the quantity is a survival-weighted expected value. [!] I PROPOSED `max_dd_r < 4.0` AS THE PROP BAR AND THAT IS WITHDRAWN. It is a risk-avoidance constraint on a problem that is not about avoiding risk, and it would have refused exactly the high-variance legs this account exists to buy a lottery ticket on. [!] AND MY SUPPORTING ARGUMENT WAS ALSO WRONG, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL CORRECTION: I said 1.5% sizing against a 6% static DD 'makes almost nothing fit'. THE BARRIER RATIO IS INVARIANT TO SIZING. At risk_pct 1.5: DD room 6%/1.5% = 4.0R, profit target 10%/1.5% = 6.67R, ratio 1.667. At 0.5%: 12.0R and 20.0R, ratio 1.667. Both barriers scale together, so cutting risk_pct does not change the ratio at all; it helps only through the second-order effect that more trades to either barrier let positive drift accumulate against variance. With trend_donchian_eth_prop's expectancy of +0.042R/trade, +6.67R is ~159 trades of drift against 4R of room, so variance dominates heavily -- whether smaller sizing raises P(success) is a COMPUTABLE QUESTION and I should not have asserted it in either direction. [!] TWO FEATURES OF THIS ACCOUNT MAKE THE EV BETTER THAN A NAIVE ABSORBING-BARRIER MODEL, both CONFIRMED in config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml: (1) drawdown_type is STATIC -- 'off the STARTING balance; NOT trailing and NOT locked/raised on payout' -- so every dollar of profit is PERMANENT cushion and the account gets monotonically safer as it wins; survival is front-loaded. (2) min_trading_days 0 and max_eval_days null -- no time pressure, can clear in one trade, so there is no forced-pace term. STRUCTURE: $45 (0.9% of the $5,000 account) buys a shot at +10% ($500) before -6% ($300); clearing converts to a funded account paying 80/20 on subsequent profits under the same static limits. So E[value] = P(clear eval) x E[lifetime payout | funded] - $45. [!] SELECTION CRITERION, AND IT IS NOT net_R: maximise P(reaching the target before the floor). A leg with LOWER expectancy but tighter loss clustering beats a higher-expectancy leg whose losses arrive in lumps. And it is a PORTFOLIO question, not a per-leg one -- legs whose drawdowns are uncorrelated smooth the path to the barrier. [!] NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH R8: the operator chose NO concentration cap for bybit_2, and correlation is nonetheless load-bearing HERE, in the opposite direction -- on prop it is not a risk limit, it is the mechanism that raises P(survival). [!] THIS RETROACTIVELY EXPLAINS THE _prop EXIT GEOMETRY, which nobody wrote down: tp_r 6.0 vs 50.0, trail_mult 3.5 vs 5.0, stale_exit_bars 12, trail_decay_stall_bars 10 / tight_mult 1.8. Capping the upside at 6R and cutting dead trades is exactly what raises P(hit +6.67R before -4R) at the cost of expectancy. Someone built the right thing for the right reason and recorded neither, so it read as an arbitrary divergence between prop and bybit -- which is what the operator asked about today. [!] THE ACTUAL GAP IS A MISSING MEASUREMENT, NOT A MISSING CONSTRAINT: MEASURED 2026-09-22, none of the 52 records under comms/strategy_evidence/ carries a per-trade R series or ANY path statistic (keys are basis, config_fingerprint, cost_stack, coverage_state, decision_rule, expectancy_r_oos, fold_detail, folds, folds_positive, n_trades_oos, net_r_oos, net_r_oos_fee_only, omitted_levers, param_selection_provenance, window_days -- no drawdown of any kind), and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py never reads one. fold_detail gives only a per-fold SUM over months, which is not an equity path. DELIVERABLE: emit the per-trade OOS R series (or a sufficient path summary) so P(target before floor) is computable per leg AND per candidate portfolio, then register that rule BEFORE using it. [!] WHAT I COMPUTED FROM fold_detail AND ITS LIMIT, kept because it is what prompted the reframe: 13 of the 42 legs with fold detail have a single fold worse than -4R, and BOTH legs live on breakout_1 are among them while both are marked `pass` (trend_donchian_eth_prop worst fold -5.3884R on total +7.13). That is NOT evidence of a breach -- a fold's net_R is a sum over months, not a contiguous drawdown -- and under this row's bar it would not be disqualifying even if it were. It is evidence only that the bar cannot see the path.

items.title: NO surface anywhere answers 'what roster has the running trader actually loaded' — every one of them re-reads the YAML
items.note: FOUND 2026-09-22 by the manager at close-out, while trying to establish what would move R2 and B2 from `landed_unproven` to `done`. It turns out nothing can, today. [!] READ FROM THE CODE, NOT THE PROSE. (1) /api/bot/config's per-account mode field is literally named `yaml_mode` -- honest naming, and it means the payload reports the FILE on the VM. (2) The payload's `trading_mode` block carries a note asserting `live_per_account is the pipeline's runtime view`, which is STRONGER THAN WHAT THE CODE DOES: that value comes from runtime_status.json, written by the live pipeline on every tick via src/web/runtime_status.py::build_status -- and build_status computes it as `_read_live_per_account(accounts_yaml)`, which OPENS AND PARSES config/accounts.yaml. (3) The same file's `strategies` field is `_read_strategy_names(strategies_yaml)`, which opens and parses config/strategies.yaml. [!] SO THE ONE ARTIFACT THE TRADING PROCESS ITSELF WRITES REPORTS THE CONFIG FILE, NOT ITS OWN LOADED STATE. `the pipeline wrote it` is not `the pipeline is using it`, and every reader has been taking the first for the second. The genuine process facts in that file are bot_uptime_s and git_sha; the roster and the per-account mode are not among them. [!] WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY, ON A LIVE-MONEY SYSTEM: a roster edit is not live until the trader reloads config. Between the merge and that reload, a leg the evidence bar just CUT is still trading real money, and there is no way to tell -- every surface shows the cut. R2 (Tier-3, 4 legs cut from bybit_2 / bybit_portfolio / breakout_1) and B2 (alpaca_portfolio 14 -> 2) are both `landed_unproven` for exactly this reason, and both would close the moment such a surface existed. Same defect class as E22: a reading surface structurally unable to express the state that matters. [!] DELIVERABLE: make runtime_status.json (or a sibling) report the roster the process HOLDS -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry -- beside the file-read values, with the two DISTINGUISHABLE and a `config_reloaded_at` stamp so `pending_reload` is a readable state rather than an invisible one. Then fix /api/bot/config's note, which currently claims a runtime view it does not have. Tier 2: it changes what a live service publishes. [!] DO NOT `fix` this by deleting the note and leaving the gap -- the note is wrong because the capability is missing, not the other way round.

items.title: The verification mapping — how we establish what is ACTUALLY trading, layer by layer, with which layers we do not have
items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to be able to verify what's actually trading... it's being operated from our VM, which means there is a single source of truth -- whatever the VM is using is de facto the single source of truth for what's actually trading. And if we can't verify that, then we need to build the mechanism to verify that... there's no reason that that question should just stay open-ended.' AGREED. This row is the mapping, and it exists because I tried to verify R2's cut this session and COULD NOT. [!] THE SIX LAYERS, IN DESCENDING AUTHORITY, EACH WITH WHETHER IT IS READABLE TODAY. (1) THE BROKER -- what positions and orders actually exist at Bybit/Alpaca. Highest authority; nothing on the VM can override it. Readable via /api/bot/positions (unrealizedPnlSource distinguishes broker truth from a local mark) and /api/bot/pnl/broker-truth. AVAILABLE. (2) REALISED BEHAVIOUR -- what the system has actually closed. /api/bot/trades/closed, keyed on `pattern` and `account`. AVAILABLE, and it is the only layer that proves a leg TRADED rather than was configured to. (3) DECISION-LEVEL EMISSIONS -- /api/bot/order-packages and /api/bot/signals. PARTIALLY BROKEN, see the measurements below. (4) THE PROCESS'S LOADED STATE -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry. NOT AVAILABLE AT ALL; this is row E31, and it is the layer the operator's question actually needs. (5) THE FILE ON THE VM -- /api/bot/config, whose mode field is honestly named `yaml_mode`. AVAILABLE, and it is what every reader has been mistaking for layer 4. (6) GIT main. AVAILABLE, and the furthest from the truth. [!] MEASURED THIS SESSION, AND THE HEADLINE IS THAT BEHAVIOURAL VERIFICATION CANNOT WORK FOR A REAL-MONEY BOOK AT TODAY'S TRADE RATE. Population: the 200 most recent closed trades, closedAt 2026-09-13T20:55:29Z -> 2026-09-22T08:48:49Z, about 9 days. Of those, 199 are PAPER and 1 is REAL MONEY -- a single bybit_2/xrp_pullback_2h trade closed 2026-09-14T18:21:48Z, EIGHT DAYS AGO. Trades closed after R2's cut: 2, both bybit_1 (paper), both ict_scalp_*. So when I asked `did any cut leg trade after the cut`, the answer was NONE -- and THE POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED, because no real-money leg traded after the cut either. A negative from a probe whose positive control is silent proves nothing. At a base rate near 0.1 real-money trades/day you would wait weeks for a behavioural answer, and layer 4 is therefore NOT OPTIONAL -- it is the only layer that can answer the question for real money on any useful timescale. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN LAYER 3 WHILE BUILDING THIS, BOTH THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS. (a) /api/bot/order-packages?limit=201 returns `rows: []` with `count: 0` -- NOT an error and NOT a clamp to the 200 cap. An over-limit request is INDISTINGUISHABLE from `there is no data`, on a read surface the SPA uses. Verified by bisection: limit 50/100/200 return 50/100/200; 201 and 250 return 0. (b) /api/bot/order-packages' newest row is 2026-09-18T15:16:46Z, four days stale, while closed trades exist from today -- so the decision-level surface is NOT tracking what the system is actually doing. (c) /api/bot/signals returns 0 rows under EVERY shape tried (bare, limit=5, limit=50, hours=720, limit=50&hours=2000 -- an 83-day window). I could NOT establish whether that is `no signals` or `a broken read`, and I am not guessing; that distinction is the same defect this row exists to remove. [!] DELIVERABLE: a single documented procedure -- one command or endpoint -- that answers `what is the running trader actually trading right now, and does it match main?`, returning each layer separately with its own read-state, NEVER collapsing `we could not look` into `nothing found`, and REFUSING to return a verdict when the positive control for a behavioural layer is silent. Depends on E31 for layer 4. [!] AND A RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF IT: a Tier-3 roster change is not `done` when the file changes; it is done when layer 4 agrees with layer 6. R2 and B2 are both sitting in exactly that gap right now. [!] OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-09-22, and it narrows this row: 'the roster is not a behaviour-observable fact, it is a LIST-observable fact based on the list that is the single source of truth. Just because something's not trading doesn't mean it's not on the roster -- it could just be sidelined. The only problem we would notice is if we see something trading that's NOT on the roster.' CORRECT, and it means I built the wrong check first. The roster question is answered by READING THE LIST THE VM IS CONFIGURED WITH, not by watching for trades; absence of trading is not absence from the roster, and my behavioural probe was testing a proposition the roster does not make. THE LAYER-2 CHECK IS THEREFORE AN INVERSE ANOMALY DETECTOR, NOT A CONFIRMATION: alert when a leg that is NOT on an account's list closes a trade on it. That is a positive assertion, it needs no positive control, and it fires on the thing that actually matters. [!] AND THE OPERATOR'S SECOND HALF IS THE REAL SPEC: the VM's configuration is the single source of truth and is NOT prescriptive -- so there should be no discrepancy between the list the VM holds and what it routes, and IF THERE IS, THAT IS A BIGGER PROBLEM. So layer 4 (E31) is not there to second-guess the roster; it is there to detect that the process and the file have diverged at all. The measurement that made me build the behavioural check -- 199 paper / 1 real money over 9 days -- was still worth having: it is not a roster fact, it is row E33.

blocked_on.what: E34 is the first-principles review the operator asked for and it may change the shape of this build -- in particular whether a global election is needed at all, given the pairs sleeve does not route through multi_account_execute. Do not write the diff before E34 reports.

items.note: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to fix the fanout mechanism'. [!] THE FAN-OUT IS A WORKAROUND LAYERED ON THE GLOBAL ELECTION, NOT A FIX OF IT, and it says so itself -- src/runtime/pipeline.py:1088: 'Per-account arbitration fan-out ... so an account whose own candidate lost the GLOBAL election is no longer dropped by `pkg.strategy in assigned` and silenced without a journal row.' The global dispatcher picks ONE winner per symbol across all accounts and then fans out; any account whose own candidate lost is dropped silently. The fan-out repairs that damage after the fact. It solves nothing the global dispatcher could not have avoided by not creating the problem. [!] AND THE STATED BLOCKER TO FIXING IT PROPERLY IS ALREADY OBSOLETE -- THIS IS THE FINDING. The reason given for never making the election per-account is that a per-account aggregator would re-emit a `regime_hard_gate` row per account per tick, corrupting the signal that partitions `would have gated` from `did gate`. But intent_multiplexer.py:876 ALREADY SPLITS GATE FROM ELECT, in a comment that says exactly why: 'Gate ONCE, then elect. aggregate_intents is exactly this composition, but spelling it out is what lets the per-account fan-out below elect N times off the SAME gated set without re-emitting a regime_hard_gate row per account per tick.' `_gated, _pre_gate = gate_intents(intents, symbol=symbol)` then `elect_from_gated(_gated, ...)`. THE MACHINERY TO ELECT PER ACCOUNT WITHOUT CORRUPTING THE AUDIT SIGNAL IS IN THE FILE AND IN USE TODAY. The fan-out is the existence proof. [!] THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: call elect_from_gated per account off the one gated set and dispatch the union, instead of electing once globally and scoping a repair round. Then there is no global winner to starve anyone, ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS becomes unnecessary, and the failure mode measured today -- a partial allowlist SUBTRACTING accounts from rounds they had won -- cannot exist because there is no allowlist. [!] TODAY'S ALL-11 ALLOWLIST IS SCAFFOLDING, NOT A SETTLED DESIGN. It removes the subtraction; it leaves the global election underneath it (BL-20260827) untouched. [!] TIER 3 -- it changes live routing on real-money accounts. Prove it against the same test the E33 lane wrote (tests/test_arbitration_fanout_allowlist_scope.py, which asserts TODAY'S DEFECTIVE BEHAVIOUR on purpose so the fix has to flip it CONSCIOUSLY); flipping those assertions is part of the deliverable and must be visible in the diff.

[!] MEASURED CAUSE, not inferred: I recomputed the fingerprint three ways. The record's digest matches the COMMITTED config EXACTLY (74242b93 == 74242b93). The only field my edit changed is `execution: shadow -> live`. So the flip ALONE moved the digest. build_strategy_evidence.py::config_fingerprint digests the ENTIRE leg config block -- json.dumps(cfg, sort_keys=True) -- which includes the execution gate. [!] THEREFORE ANY PROMOTION INVALIDATES ITS OWN EVIDENCE AT THE MOMENT OF PROMOTION. B1 landed 2026-09-21 and this is the first promotion attempted since; the defect has been latent for a day and would have blocked every one. [!] THE FIX IS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT A WEAKENING: fingerprint the STRATEGY PARAMETERS the backtest measured, excluding `execution` (and almost certainly `enabled`) -- neither is a strategy property and neither changes what a harness would produce. A moved atr_stop_mult, entry_z or lookback must still invalidate the record, and the guard's own self-test at line 626 ('P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity', plus 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)') must keep passing so the failure branch stays proven. [!] TWO WRONG FIXES, NAMED SO THEY ARE NOT TAKEN: (a) regenerating the evidence record after the flip -- it re-runs a backtest to account for a gate change that cannot affect the result, and it teaches the next session that the answer to a guard complaint is to re-roll the evidence; (b) wiring the roster WITHOUT the execution flip -- the fingerprint stays valid and the guard passes, and you get a leg that looks promoted and trades nothing, which is the silent-inert failure mode the missing AVAXUSDT symbol nearly produced the same hour. [!] FIXED AND MERGED 2026-09-22 in #12725 (operator: 'Yes push it'). _GATE_FIELDS = {execution, enabled} excluded from the digest in BOTH scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py (the producer) and scripts/ci/check_roster_promotion_evidence.py (the guard, which re-implements rather than imports so CI does not pull the producer's research deps), each carrying a comment that the set must NOT be widened to quiet a complaint. The 52 records were migrated in a way that PRESERVES the staleness signal rather than washing it out: each was graded under the OLD scheme against origin/main:config/strategies.yaml first (NOT the working tree, which carried the branch's own execution flip and would have begged the question), and a record whose parameters had genuinely drifted would have kept its old digest and still read STALE. Result 52 migrated / 0 already-stale kept, and the diff over the records is exactly 52 changed lines, all config_fingerprint. VERIFIED: --self-test PASS including 'P6 stale config_fingerprint fails identity' and 'P6 ...while all four clauses still PASS (so identity is load-bearing)', so the failure branch stays proven; the two implementations agree over all 55 config blocks; and controls confirm a gate flip does NOT move the digest while a moved atr_stop_mult DOES. [!] `landed_unproven` NOT `done`: what closes it is the guard ARMING a promotion on main — which #12725 itself is (`armed: ada_pullback_2h -> bybit_2 [roster_add]`), so this closes with R8's own observation.

items.title: Four exit-lever arms are parked awaiting a Tier-3 decision in a register nothing surfaces — three of them for five weeks, three already measured
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'are there no decisions waiting for me?' — asked after the manager reported that ZERO rows on this register carried an operator_decision edge. That report was accurate about the field and WRONG about the world, and this row is the correction. [!] THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ONE ARM. Tier-3 decisions have been accumulating in a DOMAIN register (config/lever_reachability.json) whose `disposition: queued_tier3` state means precisely 'a correction is proposed and awaiting the operator'. Nothing reads that file into the checklist, the brief, or GET /api/bot/work/checklist. Three of the four rows were opened 2026-08-16 and have sat FIVE WEEKS. This is the parking-lot failure CLAUDE.md warns about, in a register the manager added a fifth row to this very session without noticing. [!] AND THREE OF THE FOUR ARE NOT WAITING ON WORK — THEIR MEASUREMENT IS ALREADY TAKEN. Read from the registry 2026-09-22, each figure with its population: trend_donchian_sol_4h arm 5.57 — LIVE entry-conditioned (the AUTHORITATIVE basis, population COMPLETE) 0/16, backtest 0/127 across every year 2023-2026, cap_R median 1.78 live / 1.64 backtest; the arm needs risk/entry <= 1.777% and the leg's BEST (lowest-vol) entry ever observed is 2.292%, so it is not a near-miss, it is out of range — and it is STILL filed `verdict: unmeasured`, because the session that measured it deliberately left every verdict untouched 'for consistency'. A measurement that never became a verdict is the same collapsed state as `0` meaning 'we could not look'. xrp_pullback_2h arm 4.49 — LIVE COMPLETE 2/37 (5.4%), backtest 12/204 (5.9%), cap_R median 3.03; verdict `vol_conditional`, which the legend calls 'a real design choice, not a default' — nobody has made the choice. scha_trend_long_1d arm 2.00 — no live basis obtainable (the leg was declared 2026-08-09 and the live journal holds ZERO order packages for it, a `looked_and_found_nothing` read, not a failure), backtest 54/65 = 83.1%, cap_R median 2.65 ABOVE the arm. This is the one that is probably FINE. avax_pullback_2h arm 4.86 — opened 2026-09-22 by an R8 promotion that was then WITHDRAWN the same session (fold recency, not reachability), so this leg is `execution: shadow` and is NOT in the guard's denominator; the entry is kept because the measurement is real and throwing it away would mean re-deriving it the next time promotion is considered — backtest entry-conditioned 2/45 = 4.4%, stable across both years (2025 1/14, 2026 1/31), cap_R median 3.27; live basis NOT PULLED, which is different from absent and is recorded that way. [!] WHAT AN INERT ARM COSTS, STATED SO THIS IS NOT OVER-SOLD: an exit lever that cannot arm means one REFINEMENT never fires. The leg still trades its entry, its stop and its TP. Nothing is unprotected. The cost is that a declared, Tier-3-approved lever is decoration, and — per BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP, the finding this whole registry exists to stop recurring — an inert lever is indistinguishable from an armed one that has simply not triggered yet. That is the defect, not a risk to capital. [!] MANAGER RECOMMENDATION, one per leg: trend_donchian_sol_4h -> `inert` + `recorded_inert` (the authoritative population is complete and unambiguous; recording it closes the row with no code change and no arm edit). scha_trend_long_1d -> `reachable` + `ok` on the backtest basis, or leave queued if the operator wants a live basis it cannot have for months. avax_pullback_2h and xrp_pullback_2h -> the manager pulls the live order_packages basis FIRST (both are cheap relay reads), then the operator decides on complete information rather than on a backtest proxy. [!] AND THE REGISTER GAP IS ITS OWN DELIVERABLE, SEPARATE FROM THE FOUR ARMS: whatever is decided, `queued_tier3` in a domain register must become visible. Cheapest honest fix is a check that FAILS when any domain register holds an operator-gated row that no checklist row points at — the same shape as the collapsed-state guard, and it would have caught this in August. [!] ⚠️ THE FOURTH ROW'S OWN FRAMING WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE, and the correction is worth keeping: this row was filed while avax_pullback_2h was staged for bybit_2, and the entry's `unmeasured_reason` asserted the promotion as the reason it existed. The promotion was withdrawn hours later. Corrected in config/lever_reachability.json rather than only here, because a wrong claim that merges is the repo's position. [!] OPERATOR DECIDED 2026-09-22, choosing between four options: **STRIP THE ARMS ENTIRELY** — remove the reach-gate parameter from the legs where it CANNOT FIRE, so the config stops declaring a protection that does not exist. Dispatched as a lane the same minute. ⚠️ THE BOUNDARY IS THE WHOLE TASK AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDING: 'where it cannot fire' EXCLUDES scha_trend_long_1d, whose arm 2.00 measures 54/65 = 83.1% reachable with cap_R median 2.65 ABOVE it. That lever FIRES; stripping it would remove a working protection, which is the opposite of the decision. Also excluded: uso_trend_1h (100%) and trend_donchian (100%), both verdict `reachable`. STRIPPING: trend_donchian_sol_4h 5.57 (live 0/16 COMPLETE, backtest 0/127), xrp_pullback_2h 4.49 (live 2/37 COMPLETE), avax_pullback_2h 4.86 (backtest 2/45; shadow leg, entry kept as a measurement). IN A SEPARATE, TRIVIALLY DROPPABLE COMMIT: gld_pullback_1d 5.06 and qqq_trend_long_1d 3.56, already `inert`/`recorded_inert` — the same 'cannot fire' test applies and stripping them is the follow-through of an adjudication the operator already made, but it is NOT what they were shown when they answered. [!] THE THING MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG, NAMED IN THE DISPATCH: if a consumer reads the key as `cfg.get("trail_decay_arm_r", <default>)`, REMOVING the key ACTIVATES the default — the opposite of stripping. The lane must establish that from the code before editing, not assume it.

items.title: accounts.yaml::symbols is a DATA-PULL list, not a gate — the roster is the single source for what trades, and a stale pull list is a pull-list bug, never a trading decision
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'In general, I don't get why uh, th there shouldn't be a symbol specific list for each account. That's what the strategy roster is for. It trades whatever the strategies that it's trading are trading... That's exactly the kind of double gate that just stops things from working for no reason that is completely unnecessary to anything that we're doing here.' [!] VERIFIED, AND THE OPERATOR IS RIGHT ON BOTH HALVES — it is a gate, and it is redundant. IT IS A GATE, established in code and not inferred: src/main.py:714 `_resolve_tick_symbols` builds the set of symbols the trader FETCHES CANDLES FOR from each account's `symbols:` list, NOT from its roster. A symbol absent there means no data, no signal, no order — the leg sits on the roster looking wired and trades nothing. Two other readers exist and neither is a gate: src/runtime/intents.py::supported_symbols() unions the declared symbols with a static base as a VALIDATION whitelist and fails SAFE (a config-load failure falls back to the base, never narrower), and intent_multiplexer.py:485 reads the per-STRATEGY symbols, a different field. ⚠️ intents.py:100 contradicts itself inside one sentence — 'This is a validation whitelist, not a runtime on/off gate — accounts.yaml `symbols` drives what actually trades.' Field beats comment, and here the field is main.py:714. IT IS REDUNDANT, MEASURED over all 11 accounts by parsing config/accounts.yaml and config/strategies.yaml 2026-09-22: 19 ORPHAN symbols declared that no rostered leg needs (alpaca_live 8, alpaca_portfolio 7, bybit_2 1, bybit_portfolio 1, ib_live 1, oanda_practice 1), and 0 MISSING. ⚠️ READ THE ZERO CORRECTLY — IT IS NOT REASSURANCE, IT IS THE NEAR-MISS. It reads 0 only because the R8 promotion checked symbol coverage BEFORE the edit: avax_pullback_2h was about to join bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) while AVAXUSDT was absent from its list. Caught by looking, not by any guard — nothing in CI asserts the relationship, so the next one is caught by noticing silence, which is exactly how this class of defect is normally found: late. [!] AND THE FIX IS ALREADY HALF-WRITTEN IN THE SAME FILE: src/main.py:267 `_symbols_for_account` ALREADY derives the union of an account's roster symbols — it simply is not what _resolve_tick_symbols consults. [!] PROPOSED (Tier-2, additive, cannot narrow): _resolve_tick_symbols unions the roster-implied symbols into the declared ones, so the ROSTER is the single source and `symbols:` degrades to an additive override for anything a roster cannot imply. Nothing that trades today stops trading — the change can only ADD symbols to the fetch set. Plus a CI check that a rostered leg's symbol is always reachable, so the AVAXUSDT case fails a build instead of failing quietly. [!] THIS IS NOT THE 'no third gate' RULE BEING RESTATED — IT IS AN INSTANCE OF IT. CLAUDE.md § 'The two execution gates' says 'never hide a capability behind a default-off flag (the pattern that stranded MES)'. A symbol list that must be edited in a second place to let a rostered leg trade is that pattern wearing different clothes, and it stranded a leg today. [!] OPERATOR REFRAMED IT 2026-09-22 AND THE REFRAME IS SHARPER THAN THIS ROW WAS, verbatim: 'There are two separate issues here. There's the issue of what trades on what account and what data gets pulled from the account, and those are two separate things that aren't dependent. Obviously anything that's trading will need to be pulling the data, but we can still continue pulling data... for other things even if they're not being traded. But that shouldn't be formatted as a gate. That should just be formatted as additional data pulls unrelated to the strategies themselves. So we do need to find a way to union that so that we're not doing double declarations. But it also needs to make sure that the data-pull roster is not going to interfere with the strategy roster. And even if something is for some reason missing from the pull list, it doesn't mean that it shouldn't be traded — it means that the pull list is not updated correctly.' [!] SO THE SPEC IS FOUR PROPERTIES, not 'remove the second list': (1) the STRATEGY ROSTER decides what trades, full stop; (2) `symbols:` becomes a pure ADDITIVE data-pull list and it is LEGITIMATE for it to carry symbols nothing trades; (3) fetch set = UNION(roster-implied, declared), so no double declaration; (4) a symbol missing from the pull list is a PULL-LIST BUG, never a reason a rostered leg does not trade — and the CI check's FAILURE MESSAGE must say that, in those terms. [!] THIS CHANGES THE DISPOSITION OF THE 19 ORPHANS: under the reframe they are LEGITIMATE data pulls, not drift to clean up. The lane is fenced off them. My earlier framing called them redundancy; that was the one-list reading and the operator's two-concern reading is better. Dispatched as a lane, Tier-2, landing hold.

items.title: First-principles review of the arbitration mechanism — what problem did it solve, and does it still?
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-22, verbatim: 'this fanout was a solution to a bug that came into being when we started trading pairs and needed hedge mode - the solution created new problems, nor am I sure that it solved what we wanted it to. We need a bigger review of the original problem and the mechanism to be [sure] we're maintaining expected trading behavior.' [!] THIS IS A REVIEW, NOT A PATCH, and it exists because today produced two mitigations and zero answers about the mechanism itself. Three questions IN ORDER, and the third is the product: (1) what was the original problem -- established from commits and rows (BL-20260821-PAIRS-SOL-ETH-STRANDS-ON-EVERY-OPEN, BL-20260827, bybit_position_mode.py, config/pairs.yaml, the git history of aggregate_intents), not from recollection; (2) DID THE MECHANISM SOLVE IT -- not `was it shipped` but `did the broken thing stop being broken`, measured, and `nobody ever checked` is an admissible and likely answer; (3) what does it cost and is expected trading behaviour maintained. [!] THE OBSERVATION THAT MAY UNDO THE PREMISE, handed to the lane: config/pairs.yaml gates an ISOLATED 2-leg order path -- src.units.strategies.pairs_executor.run_pairs_tick, called once per tick from src/main.py, NOT via multi_account_execute. If the pairs sleeve does not go through the multiplexer at all, then the multiplexer is carrying a global constraint on pairs' behalf for no reason, and the whole mechanism may be answering a question nobody asked. [!] THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE STRUCTURAL FIX IS CHEAP OR EXPENSIVE: plan_per_account_election's docstring claims a per-account aggregator 're-emits a regime_hard_gate row per account per tick, corrupting the one signal that partitions `would have gated` from `did gate`'. That is the stated reason nobody has simply made aggregate_intents per-account. Establish whether it is a REAL constraint or a solved one. [!] AND IT MUST WRITE `EXPECTED TRADING BEHAVIOUR` AS A TESTABLE PROPERTY -- from the operator's own directive: bybit_1 runs everything (soak, paper, with fees) and must NEVER constrain another account; bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio trade the same things. Something a guard could check. [!] CHANGES NO RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR. Tier-3 subject matter, landing hold.
